concept_summary: Casements, an existing restaurant at 2351 Mission St with a Type 47 license since 2019, proposes to add outdoor seating with alcohol service in the parking lot on the same parcel.

overall.line: Of the 5 approvals this concept needs: 1 further review (zoning and use), 3 insufficient information (alcohol licence, building permit and change of use, outdoor seating or activity area), 1 allowed (health permit).
overall.next_step: Request a pre-application meeting with San Francisco Planning to confirm whether the outdoor seating addition qualifies under Planning Code § 202.2(a)(7) limits or requires a Conditional Use Authorization, and whether it is read as enlarging a conditional use.

filing_playbook.action: Schedule a pre-application meeting with San Francisco Planning to determine whether the outdoor seating addition requires Conditional Use Authorization or qualifies under Planning Code § 202.2(a)(7).
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Explain that Casements is an existing restaurant at 2351 Mission St with a Type 47 license since 2019, last approved by Planning in December 2019 as a Bona Fide Eating Place. The proposal is to add outdoor seating in the parking lot on the same parcel, with alcohol service. Ask whether this is read as enlarging a conditional use under § 178, whether the Mission SUD expansion rule in § 249.60(c)(3) applies to a Bona Fide Eating Place, and whether the outdoor area can proceed under § 202.2(a)(7) if it operates 9 a.m.–10 p.m. with seated service only and alcohol dispensed inside or by wait staff. Confirm in writing before filing.

filing_playbook.action: If Planning confirms the outdoor area qualifies under § 202.2(a)(7) and no Conditional Use is required, submit a health permit application to San Francisco Department of Public Health for the outdoor seating expansion.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: State that the outdoor area meets all § 202.2(a)(7) limits: ground level, hours 9 a.m.–10 p.m., not operated in association with a Bar use, seated areas only with no standing, and alcohol dispensed only inside the premises or by wait staff at the patron's outdoor seat. DPH will route the application to Planning for zoning review under the Interagency Permit Referrals process; Planning will confirm the outdoor area is permitted.

filing_playbook.action: Apply for a health permit to operate from San Francisco Department of Public Health, Environmental Health Branch.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Submit the application online with the Business Account Number (BAN), Location ID (LIN), and federal tax ID. Confirm that a certified food safety manager is on staff (required before the permit is issued).
filing_playbook.verification_note: Cut down to the part the cited record states.

filing_playbook.action: If a building permit is required for outdoor construction (furniture, railings, or changes to the parking lot surface), file a building permit application with San Francisco Department of Building Inspection, routed to Planning under § 175(a).
filing_playbook.what_to_say: State that the outdoor seating area is in the parking lot on the same parcel as the existing restaurant at 2351 Mission St. If Conditional Use was obtained, cite the CUA case number and attach the approval. If proceeding under § 202.2(a)(7), state that the outdoor area meets all limits and no discretionary approval was required. Provide site plans and construction drawings. Planning will review for zoning compliance.

timeline_cost.notes: No time or cost range is given because the entitlement pathway is not established. The zoning row says further review is required: enlarging the existing restaurant triggers Conditional Use under Planning Code §§ 178 and 249.60(c)(3), and whether the outdoor area meets the § 202.2(a)(7) limits (which would allow it as of right) is not established. If Conditional Use is required, expect 4–10 months including pre-application meeting, environmental review, Planning Commission hearing, and appeal period. The one comparable outdoor seating CUA at 2323 Mission St (73 m away) took 268 days. If the outdoor area qualifies under § 202.2(a)(7), the health permit (14–45 days, $470–$1,000) is the primary step. A pre-application meeting with San Francisco Planning is required to settle the pathway before any time or cost estimate can be given.
timeline_cost.path: Conditional Use Authorization (Planning Code § 303); Health permit to operate

records_summary: 2351 Mission St operates as an existing restaurant with an active ABC Type 47 license (issued October 2019), and the records confirm restaurant use here since at least 1998. The property lies in the Mission Street NCT zoning district where restaurants are a conditional use, and sits within the Mission Alcoholic Beverage Special Use District—however, the SUD permits restaurants operating as bona fide eating places to serve alcohol, and the district allows license transfers. The immediate block is dense with food and beverage businesses: 19 registered establishments within 500 ft, 11 active on-sale ABC licenses within 500 ft, and 46 licenses within 1,000 ft. The project adds outdoor seating with alcohol service to an existing licensed restaurant, which the pathway rules read as no change of use.
data_gaps: The records do not show how many eating and drinking uses currently exist in the Mission NCT district against the 167-unit cap in Planning Code Table 754
No hearing transcripts or conditions of approval are extracted for the outdoor seating CUA at 2323 Mission St
ABC license conditions for the Type 47 at this address are not exposed in the data
The base rate count (N=5) is too small to provide a statistically meaningful approval rate for comparable projects
No entertainment permits on file at this address, so the records cannot confirm whether recorded music or limited live performance has been formally permitted
The records do not show whether the parking lot outdoor area will require Planning approval for outdoor alcohol service or a change to the site layout
